quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: What should you do first when parallel parking between two cars?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop next to the car in front of your desired spot. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Change to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If possible, change to another lane to create a gap. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them enter safely.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to move.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. This protects you if another car hits you from behind — you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must make a complete stop. Then proceed when the road is clear.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you are going, then go.
Let all vehicles that arrived before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before going.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, make a complete stop and check for traffic in all directions before going.

questions.question: When an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: A traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop immediately.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing without warning signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks for trains before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for it to pass.

questions.question: When should you slow down on a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Before you enter the exit ramp.
After you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you drive?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before reaching the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: You are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, continue through the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
Passing on the right is allowed when the road ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is allowed when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is allowed when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side of the road means you can cross it to pass other vehicles when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken or dashed yellow line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a curbed street, set your parking brake and turn the steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel to the left.
Turn the steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: When skidding on a wet or icy road, release the accelerator, do not brake, and steer in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Firmly pump your brakes.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. Your car will stop faster and you can still steer.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop ahead.
Buggy warning.
Limited parking.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming ahead and you should be ready to stop.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If the rear of your car is skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle starts to skid, release the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front and rear in line, straightening out your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to guide you.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
You only need to know the general location of your destination.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar area. Don't start with only a rough idea of where you're going. Check the location on a map before you leave.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side where traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see oncoming traffic in the nearest lane.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have left the pavement edge. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back onto the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently. Wait until your speed drops, check traffic, and look for a safe place to return to the road. Don't jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter other lanes.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop because the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and cautiously through the intersection. Look both ways to check for traffic.
